ThingDef.label: pod worm
ThingDef.description: Though large and intimidating, the appearance of this strange insectoid-like creature does not match with its otherwise passive nature. While it typically lives in insectoid hives as a part of the glow pod producing caste, it occasionally wanders off or gets captured and sold by humanoids.

ThingDef.label: royal rhino beetle
ThingDef.description: A gigantic type of rare beetle that is revered by certain underground cultures for its rarity and power. While its royal purple chitin is beautiful, it is also extremely durable. The extremely sharp horn gracing their head fetches a high price. While normally gentle by nature, it is extremely dangerous when enraged.

ThingDef.label: yooka
ThingDef.description: A towering hunchbacked mammal closely related to camels and llamas. With little to no natural predators, it grazes among the taller fungi with an unconcerned grace.

ThingDef.label: pustule hornet
ThingDef.description: Predatory and dangerous, these wasps release toxic gas should they be killed. They defend their hives and their queen with considerable ferocity backed up by stings laced with potent neurotoxin.\n\nThey do not reproduce outside of their hives and give very little meat or chitin.

ThingDef.label: aaroxis dendoria
ThingDef.description: Uniquely engineered for life in an underground environment, this moth has been altered to produce silk even in adulthood, at the cost of remaining wingless.

ThingDef.label: bloodletter petrel
ThingDef.description: Uniquely adapted amongst the other wild creatures in polluted environments. Rather than feeding off potentially toxic flesh or plant matter, it instead prefers to feed off the blood of its prey.

ThingDef.label: gastro toad
ThingDef.description: A funny looking toad bigger than some rabbits. It uses its sticky acidic tongue and wide maw to snag small prey. Some waster colonies tame and raise them for their meat as well as the drug-like bile they produce.

ThingDef.label: shatterjaw beetle
ThingDef.description: One of the most dangerous inhabitants of the crystal caves, the shatterjaw hunt with their large mandibles, crushing and cutting prey to pieces before feeding.

ThingDef.label: sandpillar
ThingDef.description: Similarly to some species of salamander, this colossal caterpillar stays in its juvenile state for life but remains able to reproduce despite this.

ThingDef.label: foundry pupa
ThingDef.description: The pupal form of the foundry beetle. Its body has largely liquified as it metamorphoses within. It is completely inflammable in nature.

ThingDef.label: smog caterpillar
ThingDef.description: The larval form of the smog moth. To deter predators, it uses toxic colors.

ThingDef.label: facet moth
ThingDef.description: A large moth with wings that glimmer like the facets of crystal. It flits about in dark caverns and is often captured and kept as a pet for its beauty. The females are capable of producing multiple batches of fertilized eggs from one mating period.

ThingDef.label: thrumbungus
ThingDef.description: A gigantic, fungal amalgam creature. Rumor in the UnderRim says it was created from a mix of a failed genetics experiment and the fungi that feasted on its corpse.\n\nWhile gentle by nature, it is dangerous when enraged. The strange hide that covers much of it is extremely beautiful and incredibly resistant to damage.

ThingDef.label: mutating tumorfish spawn
ThingDef.description: The first stage of the tumorfish life cycle. It is quite weak.

ThingDef.label: pustule queen
ThingDef.description: Unlike most other insect queens, this matriarch is very dangerous. She is nearly as fast as her spawn and packs a greater punch with her stings. Her stings inject a more potent version her species' neurotoxin, allowing for her swarm to quickly overpower anything living in their way.

ThingDef.label: shatterjaw pupa
ThingDef.description: The pupal form of the shatterjaw beetle. Its body has largely liquified as it metamorphoses within. It has perhaps the most durable exterior out of all known pupae.

ThingDef.label: megakrill
ThingDef.description: While much larger than traditional krill, the megakrill is nearly as harmless. It eats algae and the like from polluted ponds and rivers. Some colonies keep swarms of them in ponds as emergency food.

ThingDef.label: gembug
ThingDef.description: Commonly found in crystal caverns, the gembug is a smaller relative of the pillbug known for its gem-like exoskeleton.

ThingDef.label: bovine grub
ThingDef.description: A large grub originally from Caveworlds, this bug is often kept in farms for the milk-like substance it produces as an adult. It is the larval form of the bovine beetle.

ThingDef.label: foundry beetle
ThingDef.description: While herbivorous, this beetle is no easy prey. It uses its massive mandibles to crush both rival mates and anything that tries to hunt it. These beetles are often bred as war bugs by the more vicious cave dwellers.

ThingDef.label: bloodrop moth
ThingDef.description: The adult form of this species. It flies near silently through cave systems in search of blood it can drain from prey using its razor sharp proboscis. Much like bats, they live in large groups.\n\nEven a small group of them can drain a large animal to death in mere minutes.

ThingDef.label: maxolotl
ThingDef.description: These large salamanders prefer wet environments with pools of water they can comfortably slip into. While they lack teeth, their strong jaws can crush the shells of most insects. They are capable of fertilizing multiple batches of eggs in one go.

ThingDef.label: fleece spider
ThingDef.description: Small and fluffy, these spiders have become a popular pet amongst the cavern-dwelling populace. It can be easily fed from whatever food falls onto the ground.

ThingDef.label: royal rhino grub
ThingDef.description: A gigantic larva of the royal rhino beetle. It is much weaker than its adult form, often remaining reclusive until fully grown.

ThingDef.label: bloodrop pupa
ThingDef.description: The pupal stage of the bloodrop moth. It uses the nutrients it gained from blood as a larvae to survive, which also causes its deep red color. While quite vulnerable in this life stage, they are not entirely defenseless, as their pupa exterior is quite hardened.

ThingDef.label: bovine pupa
ThingDef.description: A large beetle, commonly found in dark, damp places. Milkable.\n\nA large beetle originally from Caveworlds, this bug is often kept in farms for its production of a milk-like substance.

ThingDef.label: jewel pupa
ThingDef.description: The pupal form of the jewel beetle. Its body has largely liquified as it metamorphoses within.

ThingDef.label: diggerpede
ThingDef.description: The predatory diggerpede is found below the desert surface, burrowing in the sand and soil faster than most can run. It hunts anything it can lay its mandibles on when it hungers.\n\nDespite being similar to other arthropods, it gives live birth rather than lay eggs.

ThingDef.label: moss grub
ThingDef.description: A large beetle commonly found in dark, damp places, it feeds off low underbrush in caverns. While not the best source of meat, it works when little else is available.

ThingDef.label: moss pupa
ThingDef.description: A large beetle, commonly found in dark, damp places.\n\nIt feeds off low underbrush in fungal forests and while not the best source of meat, it works when little else is available.

ThingDef.label: mutating tumorfish
ThingDef.description: The adult form of the tumorfish. Now adapted to an amphibious lifestyle, it can hunt in water as well as on land. Despite still being quite fishy, it can move with surprising dexterity out of water.

ThingDef.label: facet pupa
ThingDef.description: The pupal form of the facet moth. While immobile, its hard shell protects it from most predators.

ThingDef.label: aaroxis dendoria pupa
ThingDef.description: Even in their pupal stage, their red abdomen can be seen as they metamorphose. They are almost entirely immobile in this stage.

ThingDef.label: smog pupa
ThingDef.description: The pupal form of the smog moth. While immobile, its hard shell and terrible taste protects it from most predators.

ThingDef.label: moss beetle
ThingDef.description: A large beetle, commonly found in dark, damp places.\n\nIt feeds off low underbrush in fungal forests and while not the best source of meat, it works when little else is available.

ThingDef.label: mutating tumorfish fry
ThingDef.description: The second life stage of the tumorfish. It is now bigger and omnivorous, strong enough to hunt when necessary.

ThingDef.label: mantrap
ThingDef.description: Massive compared to its progenitor, the venus flytrap, the mantrap is named such due to its ability to snag prey the size of humans. This variant has managed to develop proto-feet and can move very slowly to more food-rich environments. This all tends to terrify people.

ThingDef.label: glowtail
ThingDef.description: A small lizard adapted to toxic environments, it uses its glowing tail tip to lure in flying insects to eat. It's considered rather cute by denizens of polluted lands and is often kept as both pet and pest control, much like a cat.

ThingDef.label: royal rhino pupa
ThingDef.description: A vary large and highly durable pupa. While immobile, its shell protects it from most harm.

ThingDef.label: screecher
ThingDef.description: Mutated by pollution, this corvid has gained the ability to stun its prey using its cries while it attacks. It tends to hunt in packs.

ThingDef.label: pustule hornet
ThingDef.description: Predatory and dangerous, these hornets release toxic gas should they be harmed or killed. They defend their hives and their queen with considerable ferocity backed up by stings laced with potent neurotoxin.\n\nThey do not reproduce outside of their hives and give very little meat or chitin. This variety is loyal to the domesticated queen.

ThingDef.label: bunker bug
ThingDef.description: Whether it is engineered or mutated from a wild animal is unknown, but this massive insect-like creature can use its powerful claws to rend its way through steel almost as easily as flesh and bone. It does not breed in captivity.

ThingDef.label: acid slug
ThingDef.description: Originally designed for combat, the acid slug is one of the most dangerous predators in the earthen depths due to its highly acidic slime and flesh. The bodies of its prey are melted down to the bone within its gelatinous flesh.

ThingDef.label: fungal weevil
ThingDef.description: Unlike normal fungal infestations within insects, this infestation has somehow grown into a healthy symbiosis. The insect's movements help to spread the fungal spores while its body provides the fungus a home. In return, the fungus helps its host hide within the fungal growths of the biome.

ThingDef.label: maligoat
ThingDef.description: Naturally so hideous and maligned for its looks that it makes people flinch and cringe on sight, it is not often kept as a farm animal. For those that do so however, it produces milk of a high quality not seen elsewhere.

ThingDef.label: fungal mimic mantis
ThingDef.description: A native to the fungal forest caverns, this mantis is larger than a person. It uses its fungus-covered carapace as camouflage while hunting. Unlike other mantises, they rely on their attacks injecting anesthetic and poisonous chemicals into prey.

ThingDef.label: megaphorid maggot
ThingDef.description: The larval form of the megaphorid fly. It is extremely ravenous and not very dangerous on its own, but they are rarely if ever found as such. They are most often found having burst out of an infected animal.

ThingDef.label: polluwog
ThingDef.description: The larval form of the gastro toad. It lives in the disgusting waters of polluted biomes, feeding off any detritus and plants it can reach. It often lives in large groups.

ThingDef.label: bloodrop larvae
ThingDef.description: The larval form of the bloodrop moth. It gains nutrients for growth by feeding on the blood of any large creature. A small group of them can drain even an elephant to death in minutes.

ThingDef.label: mutagenic norphea
ThingDef.description: This unique insectoid's body is so adapted to environmental toxins that it cannot survive without them. It periodically produces a liquid that can induce mutations in humans.

ThingDef.label: sand leaper
ThingDef.description: A desert rodent related to the common surface rat. While its main defense is mostly being small and quick, it has some natural chitinous armor as well.

ThingDef.label: pustule queen
ThingDef.description: Unlike most other insect queens, this matriarch is very dangerous. She is nearly as fast as her spawn and packs a greater punch with her stings. Her stings inject a more potent version her species' neurotoxin, allowing for her swarm to quickly overpower anything living in their way. The sheer bulk of her body prevents especially long active flights, forcing her to slow her movement for longer periods than drones.

ThingDef.label: smog moth
ThingDef.description: A large moth with wings with markings that glow faintly in the dark. This creature uses its bioluminescent abdomen to lure in prey.

ThingDef.Name: RSW_BiomesCore_CrabThingBase
ThingDef.label: crab
ThingDef.description: A crab

ThingDef.label: jellypot
ThingDef.description: Named the jellypot for its ability to produce insect jelly in its large thoracic sac, this rare animal is almost exclusively found near insectoid hives. Despite being farmed much like ants do with aphids, it does not seem capable of breeding in captivity.

ThingDef.label: cinnabar caterpillar
ThingDef.description: A unique species of moth larva with a spiraling body pattern rather than the normal segmented. It is thought to be a genetic anomaly from its engineered creation. The crimson-colored silk it produces is luxuriously soft.

ThingDef.label: sacapillar
ThingDef.description: Timid by nature, this larva-like bug has a large thorax filled with putrescent gasses, allowing it to move about and escape attackers while barely touching the ground. It releases these gasses when attacked, often allowing it to escape unharmed. The gasses it contains also permit it to carry large loads, and many colonies in polluted areas use them as ridable pack animals.

ThingDef.label: jewel beetle
ThingDef.description: A small yet pretty beetle native to the desert shallows. Its brightly colored shell makes it valuable for its looks.

ThingDef.label: crested dragon
ThingDef.description: Much like the prehistoric Parasaur, this lizard has a crest. The purpose is largely for display, but also allows them to make cute squeaky noises.

ThingDef.label: stoneback
ThingDef.description: These large reptile-like animals normally feed on the likes of cacti. If angered, however, their durable hide makes them quite difficult to kill.\n\nTheir longer back legs and strange appearance lends credence to the belief that they were engineered to live in arid environments. Why they live underground, however, is uncertain.

ThingDef.label: basilisk
ThingDef.description: With eyes that enrapture its prey should they gaze into them, the six-legged basilisk is both designed and named after its mythological predecessor.

ThingDef.label: crystalline caterpillar
ThingDef.description: The larval form of the facet moth. To deter predators, its body appears spiky and hard through a form of natural mimicry.

ThingDef.label: foundry grub
ThingDef.description: A small and soft grub with inflammable chitin. Unfortunately this does not last once the grub is dead.

ThingDef.label: jewel grub
ThingDef.description: Small and relatively ugly, this little grub hides among sand and rocks to avoid potential predators. It lacks any proper defenses.

ThingDef.label: imperial toad
ThingDef.description: The imperial toad is native to the cave systems below deserts on the Rim. It tends to be preyed upon quite easily but many cave dwellers have taken a shine to it as a pet due to its regal posture.

ThingDef.label: megaphorid
ThingDef.description: A glass cannon of a creature, this disgusting bug attacks animals many times its size and tends to die in the process. Unbeknownst to the attacked, they have usually been injected with the phorid's young, which will slowly devour them from the inside out. It can survive in all but the most cold and barren environments.

ThingDef.label: crystal fairy mole
ThingDef.description: Crystal plating covers the back of this mole species, offering protection from predators and hunters.

ThingDef.label: glowslug
ThingDef.description: This bioluminescent slug is easily spotted in any dark environment, both by its own species and by predators. It is a wonder how they have survived this long, let alone to such a large size.

ThingDef.label: cave lemming
ThingDef.description: This big, solitary herbivore can swiftly hop away from danger.

ThingDef.label: megapleura
ThingDef.description: A relative of the trilobite beetle, the megapleura has grown to massive proportions while living deep within the Rim's crust. While odd in appearance, it is largely harmless.

ThingDef.label: truffle mole
ThingDef.description: Thought to be related in some strange way to the truffle pigs of Earth, this mole has a specialized sense of smell, enabling it to find rare fungi.

ThingDef.label: shatterjaw grub
ThingDef.description: While its adult form can bite a man in half, this weak, squishy grub is incapable of such a task.

ThingDef.label: pustule hornet
ThingDef.description: Predatory and dangerous, these hornets release toxic gas should they be harmed or killed. They defend their hives and their queen with considerable ferocity backed up by stings laced with potent neurotoxin.\n\nThey do not reproduce outside of their hives and give very little meat or chitin.

ThingDef.label: bovine beetle
ThingDef.description: A large beetle originally from Caveworlds, this bug is often kept in farms for its production of a milk-like substance and flakes of chitin.

ThingDef.label: crystal crab
ThingDef.description: A large and powerful relative of the decorator crab, cavern crystals grow from the minerals on this crab's rocky shell. Despite its strong exoskeleton, the crystal crab hauls around this heavy shell, the reason for which is unknown. They are not known to breed in captivity.
